rounds.name: Technical Interview
rounds.description: This round lasted for about 25-30 minutes. The process began with the interviewer asking me to introduce myself, followed by a few questions related to my resume. Since I'm from Jammu and currently studying in Mumbai, they asked why I chose to come so far for my education. They also inquired about my interest in the IT sector and whether I genuinely wanted to pursue a career in this field. This was a brief conversation before the technical questions started. Next, I was asked to explain one of the projects I had listed on my resume. I selected a project and went into detail about it. The interviewer asked why I chose specific technologies for the project (e.g., "Why did you use Next.js instead of React?"). They also wanted to understand the relevance of the project: whether it had any real-life application and if it was solving a real-world problem. After that, we moved on to questions related to computer science fundamentals. I was given real-life scenarios and asked how I would solve certain problems. One question I remember was about withdrawing money from an ATM. The question was: If money is debited from your account but not dispensed by the ATM, what could be the issue and how would you resolve it? Another technical question involved synchronizing two APIs: If the result of the first API is used as input for the second, how would you avoid any errors or overlaps during this process?. Then, the interviewer asked few questions on OOPS and DBMS.

rounds.name: Technical Interview
rounds.description: The interview lasted for about 30-40 minutes. It started with the interviewer asking me to introduce myself. After hearing my introduction, he focused on my interest in machine learning and asked me to explain what machine learning is.Next, he asked how machine learning actually works and what "data" is. After that he gave me a scenario: "What if some wrong or extreme values are included in the dataset? How would you make sure the machine still gives accurate results?". After discussing machine learning, the interviewer moved on to DBMS. He gave me a table and asked me to normalize it step by step, explaining how to make the table more efficient by reducing redundancy. He also asked me about DML and DDL commands.Then he asked me one numerical question on all types of join. Next, we shifted to data structures and problem-solving. He asked me a few questions about linked lists, including how to write code to detect if there’s a cycle in a linked list and how to swap two nodes. He also asked how to swap two numbers without using extra variables. There was a pattern-printing question as well, where I had to write code to print a specific design using loops.Toward the end, the interviewer asked about my experience with competitive programming and rating as mentioned on my resume. At the end he asked about Git and GitHub.
